quests.instruction: You want to borrow a classmate's eraser. Which way of asking is the most polite?
quests.correctAnswer: 'May I please borrow your eraser?' 🙏
options: 'May I please borrow your eraser?' 🙏
'I need to use your eraser.' 😐
'Hand over your eraser.' ✋
quests.hint: Think about how you would like to be asked.
quests.explanation: Polite words like 'may I' and 'please' show respect and make people more willing to help.
quests.funFact: Saying 'please' and 'thank you' is polite in nearly every language.

quests.instruction: Your teacher is talking with another adult, and you need help. What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Wait and say 'Excuse me' at a pause 🙋
options: Call their name until they turn 📢
Tug their sleeve to get attention 👚
Wait and say 'Excuse me' at a pause 🙋
quests.explanation: Waiting for a pause and saying 'excuse me' shows patience and lets the adult finish politely.
quests.funFact: 'Excuse me' is a handy phrase for getting someone's attention kindly.

quests.instruction: A classmate asks to use your marker, but you're still using it. Which reply is polite and honest?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'm using it, but you can have it next.' 🖊️
options: 'I'm using it, but you can have it next.' 🖊️
'Ask someone else; I don't care.' 🙄
'No, it's mine and you can't have it.' 😠
quests.explanation: Explaining why you can't share right now, and when you can, keeps things friendly.
quests.funFact: Giving a reason helps people understand your answer.

quests.instruction: Two students want the same computer at the same time. What is a fair solution?
quests.correctAnswer: Take turns, using a timer 💻
options: Take turns, using a timer 💻
The tallest goes first 📏
Whoever shouts first gets it 📢
quests.hint: Fair means everyone gets a chance.
quests.explanation: A timer lets both students have the same amount of time.
quests.funFact: Sand timers, or hourglasses, were used to measure time long before digital clocks.

quests.instruction: It's a board game, and it isn't your turn. What do you do while you wait?
quests.correctAnswer: Watch and wait patiently 👀
options: Take the dice 🎯
Move the other player's piece 🎲
Watch and wait patiently 👀
quests.explanation: Waiting for your turn is fair to the other players and keeps the game fun.
quests.funFact: Snakes and ladders is a board game that began in India, where it was called Moksha Patam.

quests.instruction: How can classmates decide fairly who goes first?
quests.correctAnswer: Pick a number or draw names 🎲
options: Pick a number or draw names 🎲
Let the loudest go first 📢
Let the teacher's favorite go first ⭐
quests.hint: Choose a method that doesn't favor anyone.
quests.explanation: Chance methods like drawing names give everyone the same opportunity.
quests.funFact: Drawing straws is an old way of making a fair choice.

quests.instruction: There's one set of markers for the whole table. What is a good way to share?
quests.correctAnswer: Pass the set around and share the colors 🖊️
options: Everyone grabs the colors they like best 🙂
One person keeps the set until they're done 🏆
Pass the set around and share the colors 🖊️
quests.hint: Think about how everyone can use them.
quests.explanation: Sharing a set means everyone gets to use colors without hoarding.
quests.funFact: Sharing resources is one reason groups can achieve more.

quests.instruction: Your group is making a big poster together. How can you share the space?
quests.correctAnswer: Agree who draws in which area 🖼️
options: Agree who draws in which area 🖼️
Let one person fill it all 🦸
Everyone draws over each other 🌀
quests.explanation: Splitting the space means every member can add something without messing others' work.
quests.funFact: A class mural lets many people add to one big picture.

quests.instruction: A classmate forgot a pencil, and you have a spare. What is a kind choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Lend them the spare ✏️
options: Pretend you have no spare 🙈
Lend them the spare ✏️
Tell them to ask the teacher only 🙋
quests.hint: A small help goes a long way.
quests.explanation: Lending a spare pencil helps them start working quickly.
quests.funFact: The word 'pencil' comes from a Latin word meaning 'little tail'.

quests.instruction: Your group has different ideas for a poster. What is a fair way to decide?
quests.correctAnswer: Listen to all, then vote or mix ideas 🗳️
options: Wait until the teacher decides for you 🤷
Let the loudest person choose the plan 📢
Listen to all, then vote or mix ideas 🗳️
quests.explanation: Listening and voting or blending ideas respects all group members.
quests.funFact: Voting is a common way groups make fair decisions.

quests.instruction: One group member isn't joining in. What might help?
quests.correctAnswer: Kindly invite them to choose a job 🤝
options: Do their part for them and say nothing 😤
Leave them out so the work goes faster 🙈
Kindly invite them to choose a job 🤝
quests.explanation: An invitation can make someone feel welcome, and they may simply need a clear task.
quests.funFact: Some people need an invitation before they speak up.

quests.instruction: Which sentence encourages your teammates?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Good idea! Can we also try this?' 🌟
options: 'That won't work. Try something else.' 👎
'Fine. I'll just do it by myself.' 😤
'Good idea! Can we also try this?' 🌟
quests.explanation: Positive words keep teamwork going and make people feel valued.
quests.funFact: Sports teams often huddle to share encouragement and plans.

quests.instruction: You disagree with a classmate. Which sentence is the most respectful?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I see it differently. Can I explain?' 🗣️
options: 'That's a silly idea, and you know it.' 😒
'I see it differently. Can I explain?' 🗣️
'You're wrong and I'm right.' 👎
quests.hint: Respect the person, even when you disagree.
quests.explanation: You can disagree with an idea without insulting the person.
quests.funFact: Saying 'I think' makes a disagreement sound less like an attack.

quests.instruction: What helps most when two people disagree?
quests.correctAnswer: Listening to each other's reasons first 👂
options: Walking away and not speaking again 😠
Listening to each other's reasons first 👂
Talking louder until the other gives in 📢
quests.explanation: Hearing the reasons behind an idea helps you find a solution.
quests.funFact: Many disagreements shrink once both sides understand each other.

quests.instruction: You and a friend can't agree on the rules of a game. What can you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Find a compromise, like trying both ideas 🤝
options: Find a compromise, like trying both ideas 🤝
Quit the game and play something else 🚪
Insist your way is the only right way 😤
quests.hint: Give a little on both sides.
quests.explanation: A compromise lets both of you feel heard, and you might discover a better way to play.
quests.funFact: In a compromise, each side gives up a little to find a middle path.

quests.instruction: A classmate's books spill across the corridor floor. What could you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Help pick them up 📚
options: Help pick them up 📚
Laugh and walk on 😆
Step over them 🚶
quests.hint: A small helping hand makes a difference.
quests.explanation: Helping quickly makes the hallway clear and shows kindness.
quests.funFact: Helping others often makes helpers feel good too.

quests.instruction: A classmate is stuck on a math problem and you know how to solve it. What is a good way to help?
quests.correctAnswer: Explain the first step and let them try 🧮
options: Do the whole problem and give it back ✏️
Explain the first step and let them try 🧮
Tell them it's easy so they try harder 😏
quests.hint: Help them learn, not just copy.
quests.explanation: Explaining a step lets your classmate learn it themselves.
quests.funFact: People often understand a topic better after explaining it to someone else.

quests.instruction: A new student looks lost in the lunch room. What is a kind choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Invite them to sit with you 🍽️
options: Whisper to a friend about them 🤫
Wave and sit at a different table 👋
Invite them to sit with you 🍽️
quests.hint: Think about how it feels to be new.
quests.explanation: Being invited makes a newcomer feel welcome.
quests.funFact: A friendly hello is understood in nearly every culture.

quests.instruction: You want to join a game that classmates are playing. What could you say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Can I play too?' 🙋
options: 'I'm going to play now.' 😤
Nothing; just grab the ball ⚽
'Can I play too?' 🙋
quests.explanation: Asking politely gives players a chance to say yes.
quests.funFact: Asking first shows respect for the game already going on.

quests.instruction: The group says their team is full. What is a good response?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Okay, maybe next time.' 🙂
options: Take the ball so they have to include you ⚽
'Okay, maybe next time.' 🙂
Stay and ask again every minute 🔁
quests.explanation: Accepting a 'no' calmly keeps friendships strong and leaves you free to try something else.
quests.funFact: Friendly responses make it more likely that you'll be invited next time.

quests.instruction: Someone asks to join your game, and there's room. How can you welcome them?
quests.correctAnswer: Make space and explain the rules 🤝
options: Let them stand and watch until the end 👀
Make space and explain the rules 🤝
Tell them they're too late to learn 🚫
quests.explanation: Making room and sharing the rules helps them join in smoothly.
quests.funFact: New players can bring fresh ideas to a game.

quests.instruction: You accidentally bump into a classmate. What do you say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Sorry, are you okay?' 🙏
options: Nothing 🤐
'Watch out!' 😤
'Sorry, are you okay?' 🙏
quests.explanation: Saying sorry and checking that they're okay shows kindness.
quests.funFact: A quick apology can stop a small accident from becoming a bigger problem.

quests.instruction: A classmate is upset because their team lost. Which comment is kind?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Good try! Want to play again?' 🙂
options: 'Stop being upset; it's only a game.' 😒
'Good try! Want to play again?' 🙂
'Ha, better luck next time.' 😆
quests.explanation: Kind words help someone feel better after a disappointment.
quests.funFact: Good sportsmanship means being kind whether you win or lose.

quests.instruction: A friend said something that hurt your feelings. What is a good first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Calmly tell them how you feel 💬
options: Calmly tell them how you feel 💬
Stop talking to them forever 🤐
Say something hurtful back 😠
quests.explanation: Telling someone calmly how their words made you feel gives them a chance to understand and fix it.
quests.funFact: Many people don't realize how their words affect others until told.

quests.instruction: You don't know how to use the stapler. What do you ask?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Could you show me how to use it?' 🙋
options: 'Could you show me how to use it?' 🙋
'What does this thing even do?' 😕
Nothing; just press it and see 🤞
quests.hint: Be clear about what you need.
quests.explanation: A clear question tells the adult exactly what you want to learn.
quests.funFact: Staplers can pinch fingers, so ask for a safe way to use them.

quests.instruction: You feel unwell while the teacher is teaching. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Raise your hand and say you feel unwell 🙋
options: Walk out quietly to find the nurse 🚶
Raise your hand and say you feel unwell 🙋
Put your head down and wait for it to pass 😴
quests.explanation: Telling your teacher quickly helps you get help to feel better.
quests.funFact: Don't wait until it's worse before saying something.

quests.instruction: Which question to your teacher is the clearest?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Which page are we on?' 📖
options: 'What?' 🤷
'Which page are we on?' 📖
'I don't get it.' 😖
quests.hint: A clear question gets a clear answer.
quests.explanation: Specific questions get specific answers, so you get the right help.
quests.funFact: In Spanish, questions begin with an upside-down question mark as well as ending with one.

quests.instruction: You couldn't finish your homework because you were ill. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher before class and explain 🗣️
options: Copy a friend's homework quickly in class ✏️
Tell your teacher before class and explain 🗣️
Say nothing and hope it goes unnoticed 🤞
quests.explanation: Explaining beforehand shows responsibility, and your teacher can help you catch up.
quests.funFact: Teachers usually understand when you explain honestly.

quests.instruction: You think there's a mistake in how your work was marked. What is a polite thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Could you check this answer, please?' 📝
options: Say nothing and feel upset about it 😞
'You marked this wrong, so fix it.' 😠
'Could you check this answer, please?' 📝
quests.explanation: Asking politely lets your teacher look again and explain, and sometimes corrections are made.
quests.funFact: In many countries, students can ask for exam marks to be checked again.

quests.instruction: You need more time to finish a project. When should you ask your teacher?
quests.correctAnswer: As soon as you know you need it ⏰
options: As soon as you know you need it ⏰
After it's late, once you've finished it 🕰️
On the morning the project is due 📅
quests.hint: Think about how much time your teacher needs to help you.
quests.explanation: Telling your teacher early gives them time to plan and help.
quests.funFact: The earlier you ask, the more options you have.
